card.title: Why teenagers go to bed late

body.question: How does the body's sleep timing tend to shift during adolescence?
body.reveal: Later. In adolescence the circadian rhythm shifts so that sleep and wake times become later, and an evening chronotype is unique to this period. The CDC advises 8 to 10 hours for ages 13 to 17. Concern about teen sleep has drawn public attention, especially to school start times.

probes.question: True or false: an evening chronotype is unique to adolescence, compared with childhood and adulthood.
How many hours of sleep does the CDC advise for ages 13 to 17?
